Free Recipe Sites Directory

Genuinely free recipe sources, hand-picked and link-checked. No paywalls, no “free trial” tricks, no recipe riddled with pop-ups — just places that help you get dinner sorted.

How to flip to dinner in under a minute:

  1. Open the Tonight page if you already roughly know what your pantry can do — cook straight from it.
  2. Otherwise open the fridge / pantry search tool and type what you have.
  3. Grab a deets-packed recipe: budget blogs for the “how do I afford this”, government & extension nutrition sites for the “is this feeding my family right”, library & free archives when you want the deep cut.

Categories

  • Library & free-culture archives — public-domain cookbooks, digital library menus, and open-recipe collections. Free in the “out of copyright, permanent on a library server” sense.
  • Government & extension nutrition sites — USDA, NHLBI, and university extension recipe hubs. Genuinely free, genuinely nutritionist-reviewed.
  • Budget-cooking blogs — people who cook every night on a real grocery budget and write down what actually worked.
  • Text-first, no-photo & fast sites — zero photo essays, near-zero data. Perfect on bad connections and old phones.
  • Tonight: fridge & pantry helpers — type your ingredients, get dinner ideas.
  • The Tonight page — dinner formulas you can cook with no link open at all.

Why this exists

Most “best recipe sites” round-ups rank sites by how good they look in a screenshot. This directory ranks by a different question: can you flip to a workable dinner, tonight, for free, on a slow connection? Among other things that’s why a text-only 1998 archive sits next to a modern SNAP-Ed recipe database — both of them answer that question.

Notes

  • Every external link was live at build time and is re-checked by the included link-check script. Some libraries block datacenter traffic, so the checker treats un-fetchable-but-real sites as warnings, not failures — see the README.
  • We promote no sites. No affiliate links, no sponsored anything.
  • If a recipe site starts charging mid-browse or wants an account, close the tab — there is always a free copy of the same idea on one of these pages.

Sister projects
